messages:
maria: putting together the benchmark plan for the next perf cycle — want to validate kernel selection + batching heuristics under realistic microburst + long-tail traffic. quick sync?
vikram: +1. main ask: reproducible generator that can do deterministic ramps, configurable burst spikes, and replay mode from production traces.
sasha: important: apples-to-apples requires pinning model binary, compiler flags, and quantization. also record kernel choices per step (so we know why a perf cliff happened).
oliver: propose three modes: 1) synthetic ramp (sawtooth + gaussian jitter), 2) episodic burst replay (from sampled prod traces), 3) focused long-tail stress (heavy p99/p999 token bursts).
maria: exact metrics we need: tail latency (p95/p99/p999), tokens/sec, GPU util, kernel-switch counts, batch sizes distribution, kv cache hit ratio, and mem copies. also capture CPU-side scheduling stalls.
vikram: config sketch:
```yaml
mode: ramp
qps_profile:
  base: 10
  peak: 400
  ramp_seconds: 600
burst_profile:
  probability: 0.02
  multiplier: 8
kv_warmup: true
seed: 42
``` 
sasha: KV cache note — we should vary distribution of prefixes so some sessions reuse KV and others cold-start. add a `kv_key_ttl` and `kv_reuse_ratio` knobs.
maria: agree. also add `kernel_force` param to force specific kernel families (float16, int8 kernels) so we can isolate kernel selection impact.
oliver: for apples-to-apples: baseline-run -> record full env: commit sha, CUDA/cuDNN/driver, compiler flags, model sha, container image. then run candidate-build with same env except the variable under test.
vikram: infra-bot: can you schedule a 2-hour run on dedicated perf pool at 03:00 UTC with the above configs? label: "bench/traffic-etch-2026-03"
infra-bot: sched: job queued on perf-dedicated-3, window 03:00-05:00 UTC, id=bench-2490012345-01 :white_check_mark:
maria: plan for profiling: perf counters + nsight GPU traces for ~10% of requests (sampled) and full kernel timeline for the whole run. correlate with host perf (pmu) and trace spans.
sasha: regression detection: run A/B in back-to-back windows and compute failure if p99 regresses by >5% or GPU cycles increase by >8% for same throughput.
oliver: small smoke first: 10m ramp + a few 1s microbursts to validate instrumentation. if good, run full 2h long-tail variant.
vikram: also add deterministic seed replay endpoint so we can reproduce the exact QPS and spike timings locally.
maria: thanks — I'll draft the harness proto and a minimal CLI. will tag the PR with the run config and baseline results. :memo:
sasha: sg. I'll add kernel selection logging in the runtime (kernel family + reason: latency/cost/policy).
oliver: note: include a synthetic client that can drive both HTTP streams and grpc multiplexing — some kernels react differently to stream vs chunked input.
maria: perfect. followups: PRs for generator + perf infra + runtime-logging. aiming to land by EOD tomorrow. any blockers?
vikram: none from me. might need a preferential slot if the perf pool is busy.
infra-bot: reminder: quota for perf-dedicated-3 during maintenance window 03:00-04:00 UTC will be limited to 60% capacity. plan accordingly.
maria: noted. we'll reduce parallel clients for those minutes. thanks y'all. :rocket:
